You are auditing part of the admin portal of a real VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. READ EVERY LINE of these files (absolute paths, whole files, no sampling):

PAGES: /opt/nxeon/app/admin/billing/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/invoices/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/subscriptions/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/plans/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/coupons/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/game-plans/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/gift-codes/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/email-plans/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/products/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/affiliate/page.tsx
COMPONENTS: /opt/nxeon/components/admin/InvoiceAdmin.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/CouponControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/GiftCodeControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/GamePlanControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/EmailPlanControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/ProductTables.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/AffiliateControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/SubTabs.tsx

For EVERY control find its server action in /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-*.ts and verify the auth check is INSIDE the action. These pages are "billing" area (roles BILLING + ADMIN per lib/rbac.ts). Guards: requireArea("billing"), requireAdmin, requireArea. A control that a BILLING role sees but whose action requires only requireUser/nothing = defect. Also flag any action guarded MORE loosely than "billing" (e.g. requireUser) reachable from these pages.

Report with exact file:line:
1. Any control whose action lacks a server-side guard, or whose guard is weaker than "billing" (esp. money-moving: refund, credit, void, adjust, payout, coupon/gift creation).
2. Money paths reachable by an admin that touch a CUSTOMER's balance and are missing `assertNotImpersonating` (note: admin layout already blocks impersonation, but flag anyway).
3. Displayed financial NUMBERS (MRR, revenue, totals, counts) that are hardcoded or computed wrong / not from what they claim (e.g. summing refunds as revenue, counting deleted rows).
4. Destructive money actions (force-refund, void) without confirmation or misstating consequence.
5. Missing audit() on consequential actions.

Do NOT edit. Do NOT run node/prisma scripts. Return each page with one-line verdict (CLEAN/DEFECT) then defects as file:line + impact + the exact offending line quoted.

1	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";
4	
5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
45	  "/admin": "overview",
46	  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
47	  "/admin/users": "clients",
48	  "/admin/support": "support",
49	  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
50	  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
51	  "/admin/ips": "fleet",

56	  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
57	  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",

84	};
85	
86	export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
87	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
88	}
89	
90	export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
91	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
92	}
93	
94	/**
95	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
96	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
97	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
98	 */
99	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
100	  const user = await realUser();
101	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
102	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
103	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
104	  return user;
105	}

content.thinking:
I'm seeing that requireArea uses realUser() internally, so actions guarded by it automatically operate as the real user regardless of impersonation state. The admin layout blocks impersonation on its own, but since these money-moving actions like refundPayment and adjustBalance are network endpoints, they can be called directly and bypass the layout protection. The issue is that while requireArea returns the real user for auth purposes, these actions don't explicitly call assertNotImpersonating to prevent impersonated users from triggering them.

Looking at which admin actions actually modify customer balances: refundPayment, adjustBalance, and adminUpdatePayout all touch balance fields without assertNotImpersonating guards. The task wants me to flag these anyway, even though the layout already blocks impersonation.

Now I'm checking the financial calculations on the billing page — specifically how revenue is being computed. The revenue figure sums all negative wallet transactions, but that's problematic because negative transactions include refunds, affiliate payout cash-outs, and admin balance adjustments, which shouldn't count as revenue. So the displayed revenue is overcounting by treating these non-revenue debits as actual customer spending. Refunds are negative wallet transactions, so when I sum all negatives and negate them, refunds actually increase the reported revenue—which is backwards. Similarly, affiliate payout cash-outs (when customers withdraw referral earnings) are counted as revenue. This is a genuine defect: the revenue metric is inflating by treating refunds and payouts as positive contributions when they should reduce revenue.

I'm seeing this pattern across multiple pages. On the billing page and subscriptions page, there's another issue with how admin credits are being tracked. The "Credits issued · 30d" stat searches for transactions with "Admin credit" in the description, but it's missing credits created through the adjustBalance function because that uses a different description format. So the metric only captures credits from one code path and undercounts the actual total.

The outstanding liabilities calculation sums all user balances, which technically works but includes staff and admin accounts without filtering by role. The invoice aggregates look reasonable — issued excludes voided invoices, paid counts paid ones, and open counts open ones. The invoices page uses the same logic and appears clean. Now I'm moving to the invoice detail page. The game servers are being billed at their game plan flat price, not the base VPS plan price, so the MRR calculation is overcounting them at the base rate — that's a significant defect I should flag. Let me think through whether this is actually a material issue or just a known quirk of how the system works.

Looking at the other metrics: overdue and free counts are accurate, but lifetime revenue has the same negative-sum problem as the billing page, so I'll flag that too. The Plans page is stricter than billing with its requireAdmin check, which is fine since the task only asks me to flag looser controls. Same with the Coupons page — all three operations (create, toggle, delete) require admin and are audited, so they're all properly secured.

For Game-plans and Gift-codes, both use requireArea("billing") with audit trails and confirmation on deletes. Gift codes create prepaid credit, which appropriately falls under the billing area's scope. Everything checks out there.

On the Gift-codes page though, there's a minor issue: the outstanding value calculation sums unredeemed codes but caps the query at 500 codes. If more than 500 codes exist, both the total count and outstanding value will undercount. The display shows codes.length (capped at 500) as "Total codes," which is misleading when the actual count exceeds that limit.

Moving to Email-plans: the save, toggle, and delete operations all require the billing area and are audited—clean. Products page is read-only, and I'm checking the MRR computations now, starting with how email MRR is calculated. The payout stats are computed over the first 500 rows, which could undercount if there are more payouts. The leaderboard correctly distinguishes between all referrals and converted ones (those with rewards). Now I need to systematically check whether any money-related actions are guarded less strictly than the billing area — starting with bulk void invoices and refund payment. Finishing the remaining actions through adminSavePlan — all use requireArea("billing") or stricter requireAdmin guards with no weaker controls. Each guard is verified as the first line in the action, so no point-1 defects. Now checking which consequential actions are missing audit logs — refundPayment and adjustBalance both have them.

All consequential actions across invoices, coupons, gift, gameplans, emailplans, and admin payouts/server actions include audit logging, so no point-5 defects. For point 4, I'm checking destructive money actions for confirmation dialogs — voidInvoice, bulkVoidInvoices, and adminUpdatePayout all have confirm prompts, but refundPayment is a direct form submission that sends real money to a card with no confirmation dialog, making it a point-4 candidate. adminExtend can gift months without confirmation, creating refundable value. DeleteCoupon, DeleteGiftCode, DeleteGamePlan, and DeleteEmailPlan all have proper confirmations. So point 4 is clear: refundPayment and adjustBalance are the problematic ones—refunds push real money to a card with just a single click and no dialog. Now I'm digging deeper into point 3 about revenue, checking what negative wallet transactions exist beyond legitimate purchases. This is definitely a defect—refunds and payouts shouldn't count as revenue. I can see it's present across multiple pages in the billing and subscriptions sections. I'm also noticing a mismatch in how "Credits issued 30d" is being filtered: the code is looking for "Admin credit" in the description, but the actual adjustment descriptions use different wording like "Admin balance adjustment," so they're not being captured correctly. The refund and adjust controls are both accessible from the invoice detail page, so that's confirmed. The invoice detail page does prefill the refund amount with the full total for partially-refunded invoices, but the server validates it so that's acceptable. Now I'm organizing my findings by page: the billing page has two defects—revenue counts refunds and payouts incorrectly, and the credits-issued filter only captures the user-page credit tool while missing the billing-page adjust tool. The invoices list page looks clean with proper guards and aggregation. The invoice detail page has defects too—the refund and adjust actions lack confirmation dialogs, and they're missing the impersonation check that should protect money operations.

Continuing through the rest of the dashboard, the subscriptions page has the same lifetime revenue overcount issue plus an MRR calculation that incorrectly prices game servers at the base plan rate. The plans, coupons, email-plans, and products pages are all clean. The gift-codes page has a minor issue where totals are capped at 500 records, so anything beyond that gets undercounted. The affiliate page has a missing impersonation guard on the payout update endpoint.

Looking at the overall pattern, every control maintains the same guard strength as the billing page, and all consequential actions properly include audit logging. Time to write up the final report.

content.text:
I have everything needed. All action guards, financial computations, and control wiring have been traced. Here is the audit.

---

## Summary of guard posture (points 1 & 5)

Every control on these 11 pages resolves to a server action whose auth guard is the FIRST statement inside the action, and every guard is `requireArea("billing")` or stricter (`requireAdmin`). **No control reachable from these pages is guarded looser than "billing," and every consequential action writes `audit()`/`auditLog`.** So audit points 1 and 5 are clean platform-wide. `requireArea` (lib/rbac.ts:99-105) resolves via `realUser()`, and the admin layout redirects out of impersonation (app/admin/layout.tsx:66-67).

The real findings are in the money math (point 3), confirmations (point 4), and impersonation guards on balance-touching admin actions (point 2).

---

## Per-page verdicts

### 1. app/admin/billing/page.tsx — DEFECT

- **"Revenue · 30d" / "Revenue · all time" count refunds, wallet cash-outs and admin debits as revenue** — billing/page.tsx:21-28, rendered :96-97. The queries sum every negative `walletTransaction` and negate it:
  `db.walletTransaction.aggregate({ where: { amountCents: { lt: 0 } }, _sum: { amountCents: true } })`
  Negative rows are not only purchases. `refundPayment` writes `amountCents: -walletDebit` ("Refund — …", actions-admin-billing.ts:213), `requestAffiliatePayout` writes `-cents` ("Affiliate payout request (wallet cash-out)", actions-affiliate.ts:95-101), reinstated payouts write `-amountCents` (:179-186), and a negative `adjustBalance` writes a negative row. Each of these therefore *increases* reported revenue — a refund makes revenue go up. Impact: headline revenue figure (and the identical one on Subscriptions) is overstated by all refunds + affiliate cash-outs + admin debits.
- **"Credits issued · 30d" silently misses the billing-area's own adjust tool** — billing/page.tsx:29-36. Filter is `description: { contains: "Admin credit" }`. `adjustBalance` (the AdjustBalanceForm shown in this same billing area) writes `"Admin balance adjustment…"` (actions-admin-billing.ts:281), which does not contain "Admin credit". Only `adminCreditUser` ("Admin credit adjustment", actions.ts:937 — the Users page) matches. Impact: admin credits issued via the RefundControls adjust form are invisible in this stat.

### 2. app/admin/invoices/page.tsx — CLEAN
Guards `requireArea("billing")`; `bulkVoidInvoices` = `requireArea("billing")` + audit + confirm string (:128). Aggregates (issued excl-void / paid / open / count) are correct.

### 3. app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx — DEFECT
- **Refund and balance-adjust fire real money with no confirmation (point 4)** — the RefundControls block (invoices/[id]/page.tsx:68-72) renders RefundForm and AdjustBalanceForm (components/admin/RefundControls.tsx). The "Refund" button (RefundControls.tsx:59) submits straight to `refundPayment`, which pushes money to the customer's Stripe card / debits their wallet, with no `window.confirm`. Contrast InvoiceAdminActions Void (InvoiceAdmin.tsx:43) and PayoutStatusControls (AffiliateControls.tsx:114) which both confirm. AdjustBalanceForm "Apply" (RefundControls.tsx:96) likewise debits a customer below zero with no confirm.
- **Money paths missing `assertNotImpersonating` (point 2)** — `refundPayment` (actions-admin-billing.ts:55-59) and `adjustBalance` (:265-269) mutate `user.balanceCents` but never call `assertNotImpersonating`; they authenticate with `requireArea("billing")` (which reads `realUser`). Blocked in practice by the layout redirect, but flagged as requested since the action endpoints themselves carry no impersonation guard.

### 4. app/admin/subscriptions/page.tsx — DEFECT
- **"Lifetime revenue" — same refund-as-revenue overcount** — subscriptions/page.tsx:18-22, `totalRevenueCents = -(revenueAgg._sum.amountCents ?? 0)` (:26), rendered :38. Identical `amountCents: { lt: 0 }` sum.
- **MRR miscounts game servers at the base-VPS price** — :24-25: `mrrCents = paid.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.plan.priceCents, 0)`. A game server carries both a base `planId` and a `gamePlanId` and is billed at the game plan's flat price, not `plan.priceCents` — the codebase itself documents this exact confusion as an 80% overcharge bug in `renewNow` (actions.ts:641-644). Impact: MRR is wrong for every game server.

### 5. app/admin/plans/page.tsx — CLEAN
`adminSavePlan` = `requireAdmin` + Zod + audit (actions.ts:945-980), stricter than billing.

### 6. app/admin/coupons/page.tsx — CLEAN
`adminCreateCoupon` / `adminToggleCoupon` / `adminDeleteCoupon` all `requireAdmin` + audit (actions-growth.ts:249,303,318). Money-creating (coupon) but guarded stricter than billing; delete confirms (CouponControls.tsx:99).

### 7. app/admin/game-plans/page.tsx — CLEAN
`adminSaveGamePlan` / `Toggle` / `Delete` = `requireArea("billing")` + audit (actions-gameplans.ts:52,128,140); delete blocks while servers reference it and confirms.

### 8. app/admin/gift-codes/page.tsx — DEFECT (minor)
Guards correct: `adminCreateGiftCodes` / `adminDeleteGiftCode` = `requireArea("billing")` + audit (actions-gift.ts:51,87), delete confirms and refuses redeemed codes.
- **Stats are computed only over the latest 500 codes** — gift-codes/page.tsx:14-23 uses `take: 500`; "Total codes" (`codes.length`, :35) and "Outstanding value" (:21-23,43) are derived from that capped set. With more than 500 codes issued, both the count and outstanding-liability figure silently under-report.

### 9. app/admin/email-plans/page.tsx — CLEAN
`adminSaveEmailPlan` / `Toggle` / `Delete` = `requireArea("billing")` + audit (actions-email-hosting.ts:145,196,208); delete blocks on active subscriptions and confirms.

### 10. app/admin/products/page.tsx — CLEAN
Read-only. MRR normalizes term correctly (`monthlyCents = priceCents/termMonths`, ProductTables.tsx:43-46) and filters to live statuses. Tax panel is display-only and explicitly labels tax as not collected.

### 11. app/admin/affiliate/page.tsx — DEFECT (point 2 + minor)
Guard correct: `adminUpdatePayout` = `requireArea("billing")` + audit (actions-affiliate.ts:140-206); PAID/DECLINE confirm (AffiliateControls.tsx:135-139).
- **Balance-touching money path missing `assertNotImpersonating` (point 2)** — declining credits the customer's wallet (`balanceCents: { increment }`, :166-176) and reinstating re-debits it (:179-186); no `assertNotImpersonating`. (The customer-side `requestAffiliatePayout` *does* call it, actions-affiliate.ts:50.) Layout-blocked, flagged as requested.
- **Stats capped at `take: 500`** — affiliate/page.tsx:20-24; "Total paid out" / "Outstanding" (:40-45) under-report beyond 500 payout rows.

---

## Cross-cutting notes
- The recurring root cause behind the point-3 findings is treating "any negative `walletTransaction`" as customer revenue. Refunds, affiliate cash-outs, and admin debits all live in that same negative space and pollute Revenue on both the Billing and Subscriptions pages.
- Confirmations are inconsistent: destructive *deletes* and *voids* all confirm, but the two most consequential money movers (`refundPayment` to a live card, and negative `adjustBalance`) submit with a single click.

Relevant files: /opt/nxeon/app/admin/billing/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/subscriptions/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx, /opt/nxeon/components/admin/RefundControls.tsx, /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-admin-billing.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-affiliate.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-gift.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts, /opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts.
